summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted with sepsis from a gangrenous right foot ulcer. She initially underwent a below-knee amputation, but due to poor wound perfusion, an above-knee amputation was required. She was treated with IV imipenem for multidrug-resistant Proteus mirabilis and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Her dialysis access was transitioned from the femoral vein to a tunneled external jugular catheter to reduce infection risk. Warfarin was held perioperatively and bridged with heparin, with plans to resume outpatient anticoagulation. She developed emotional distress post-amputation, which improved with counseling support. She was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation, ongoing heparin bridging until INR therapeutic, and follow-up with vascular surgery.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities with gangrene
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Infection with drug-resistant microorganisms, unspecified, with multiple drug resistance
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
